//: The two independent provider entries, exactly as they are meant to be merged into models.entries of the application's graph.config.json. `credentials.grok` (secretRef GRAPH_SUBSCRIPTION_GROK_ACCESS_TOKEN, platform grok) and `credentials.chatgpt` (secretRef GRAPH_SUBSCRIPTION_CHATGPT_ACCESS_TOKEN) must exist; both only ever carry a secretRef, never a key. Grok answers the chat-completions contract on the xAI endpoint; ChatGPT's Codex backend answers the Responses contract only, which is why that entry names openai-responses. The ChatGPT entry names Grok as its transport fallback (`fallbackModelId`): when the Codex backend breaks the connection before answering (EOF / timeout / non-2xx), the same review turn continues on Grok, and the graph records `graph.provider.fallback` with the primary model, the failure verbatim, the fallback model and `sameModel:false`. A model that answered badly is never re-asked elsewhere.
